4. Classical Demand Theory

From indifference curves through utility maximization and the Slutsky decomposition to duality with expenditure minimization — the heart of demand theory.

  • Indifference Curves and MRS — The indifference map of Cobb-Douglas utility. Move the reference bundle and the whole map redraws; the marginal rate of substitution MRS=a1−ax2x1MRS = \frac{a}{1-a}\frac{x_2}{x_1}MRS=1−aa​x1​x2​​ at that point reads off as the tangent slope.
  • Utility Maximization — The optimum is where the budget line touches an indifference curve. Move prices and wealth and the optimum slides; the first-order condition MRS=p1/p2MRS = p_1/p_2MRS=p1​/p2​ holds at every moment, verified numerically.
  • The Slutsky Decomposition — Why does demand fall when the price rises — split into substitution and income effects. Switch between Slutsky compensation (afford the old bundle) and Hicks compensation (keep the old utility) and see how the two decompositions differ.
  • Expenditure Minimization and Duality — Achieving target utility as cheaply as possible — the tangency of isocost lines and the indifference curve. Turn on the "UMP mirror" and the utility-maximizing bundle at w=e(p,u)w = e(p, u)w=e(p,u) lands exactly on Hicksian demand. That coincidence is duality.
